topic.title: Why Google pays Apple billions a year just to be the search box on the iPhone

title: Why Google pays Apple $20B for one iPhone setting 📱
description:
Why would Google pay its biggest rival billions just for one setting on your iPhone?
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Would you change your search box? Tell me below

lines.text: You think Apple only earns from iPhones? It doesn't. Here's why.
Google paid Apple $20B in one year, for one setting. Here's what it buys.
That much money, for one setting? Which setting is worth it?
The search box. Type anything into Safari, the iPhone's browser, and Google answers first.
But Google search is free. How does paying for it make sense?
Because every search shows ads, and a shop pays Google each time someone taps one.
So what does that one deal cost Google every day?
Spread over a year, that's $54.8M a day, and $2.3M every hour.
But here's the twist. It isn't a flat fee at all. Apple keeps 36% of the ad money Google makes from Safari searches.
So every time I search on my iPhone, Apple gets a cut?
Every search that shows an ad. Google isn't paying for a setting. It's renting your habit, and the rent comes to $38,052 every minute.
Still think Apple only earns from iPhones? So, would you change your search box?
